newsitem.title: czech republic: Czech leader gets pneumonia after cancer surgery.
newsitem.headline: Czech leader gets pneumonia after cancer surgery.

text.p: Czech President Vaclav Havel has developed pneumonia following surgery to remove a malignant lung tumour earlier this week, a Czech surgeon said on Thursday.
But Dr Pavel Pafko told a news conference that tests showed no spreading of the cancer after the radical surgery which removed a small malignant tumour along with half of Havel's right lung.

"The condition of the president has become slightly complicated," Pafko said. "A slight pneumonia is starting" in the left lung, he added. "This is not very often a complication, but it sometimes happens."
Tests showed there was no metastasis after the surgery on Monday, meaning the cancer had not spread.

"The definite microscopic examination ... will be known next week. But all tests conducted showed absolutely clearly ...that nowhere has metastasis been found," said Pafko, who led the surgical team in Monday's operation.
He said a team of cancer specialists would meet again early next week to discuss Havel's progress and would decide what further treatment the president might need.
Havel, aged 60 and a heavy smoker, entered hospital on November 25 after his office said he was suffering from pneumonia.
Doctors said the cancer had been caught at an early stage and the prognosis for Havel, who helped lead Prague's non-violent 1989 revolution against communism, was good.
Pafko said it was not possible to say if the tumour resulted directly from Havel's smoking.
Havel, whose role as Czech president is more ceremonial than executive, could possibly leave hospital next week and might be back at work in about six weeks, Pafko said.
He said cancer cases such as Havel's usually did not require painful chemotherapy or radiation treatment.
"From my experience patients with such a small (cancer) discovery like Mr President's usually do not get further treatment."
Havel is recovering in the intensive care unit of Prague's Third Surgical Clinic.
